payload.rationale: To resolve YES, the 2026 annual NASA GISS LOTI anomaly must be strictly greater than 1.28 C (since it also must be above the 2025 value of 1.19 C). The sum of the anomalies for the first eight months of 2026 is 9.79 C, which is an average of approximately 1.22 C. To achieve an annual average above 1.28 C, the remaining four months (September through December) must sum to at least 5.57 C. This requires an average anomaly of roughly 1.39 C over the final third of the year. While August reached 1.40 C, the previous seven months ranged from 1.09 C to 1.32 C. Sustaining an average of 1.39 C for four consecutive months is a high hurdle, making the YES outcome unlikely. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is if the 1.40 C reading in August signals the onset of a strong El Niño or another rapid warming phase that persists through the end of the year. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is if August was merely a short-term outlier and temperatures quickly revert to the ~1.20 C average observed earlier in 2026.
limitations: The annual target remains unknown, with four months missing.
No ENSO forecast or fitted annual-temperature predictive distribution is supplied.
Small coordinator-selected packet; no fitted probability model or complete research review.
